question_text:
On January 1, 2026, X became the 21st member of the eurozone.
Rumen Radev, then President of X, resigned in January to fight an election and went on to become the Prime Minister. Radev joins the likes of Vladimir Putin of Russia and Aleksandar Vučić of Serbia, serving as both President and Prime Minister of their respective countries.
This May X won the Eurovision song contest for the first time, with the song Bangaranga performed by Dara.
ID X.
answer_text: X=Bulgaria. Bulgaria is the only eurozone member that uses the Cyrillic alphabet

question_text:
John F. Kennedy had the A built under the West Wing in 1961, after the Bay of Pigs disaster convinced him that he was getting information too slowly. This March, three weeks into the Iran war, B opened a pop-up bar on K Street in Washington called "The A", with live X feeds, flight radar, Bloomberg terminals, and a huge globe showing odds. Patrons were supposed to be able to bet on geopolitical crises in real time with their drinking buddies.
Like the Bay of Pigs invasion, it did not go well. On opening night, none of the TVs worked, and there was no betting. Wired called it a "disaster".
ID A (5 points) and B (5 points).
answer_text: A=Situation Room. B=Polymarket. The bar shut early at 9 pm on opening night. It operated for the next two nights, with intermittent technical issues

question_text:
In 1969 X shared the Academy Award for Best Actress for her role in Funny Girl, in the only tie for that award in Oscar history. She briefly tripped en route to the stage, stepping on the bell-bottomed leg of her pantsuit. Looking down at the statuette, she said: "Hello, gorgeous!" – her opening line in Funny Girl.
In 1983 X became the first woman to write, produce, direct, and star in a major studio film.
This May the Cannes Film Festival gave X an honorary Palme d'Or, but a knee injury kept her away, so Isabelle Huppert spoke in her honor and X accepted by video.
ID X.
answer_text: X=Barbra Streisand. The picture on the question page was of her mansion, the one that she sued the photographer over, leading to the term Streisand Effect

question_text:
The name X is derived from a term meaning "lord of the deer." Another historical name for the place was RshipaTTaNa ("city of sages"). X is sacred to millions of people because of events described in an ancient scripture called "The String about the Setting in Motion of the _____ of the Law," or more prosaically, "The Promulgation of the Law."
This July at the 48th session of the World Heritage Committee in Busan, South Korea, X became the 45th site from India to be inscribed in UNESCO's list of World Heritage Sites.
ID X.
answer_text: X=Sarnath, from sAranganAtha. The dharmachakrapravartanasUtra describes Gautama Buddha's first-ever sermon delivered to five former companions at Sarnath. The lion capital found at Sarnath, erected during the reign of Ashoka Maurya, is the basis for the emblem of the Republic of India

question_text:
X turns 100 in 2026. Soon after it opened, it became the primary means of escape from the Dust Bowl for desperate people. The Dust Bowl was a severe anthropogenic natural disaster that affected around 100 million acres in the Great Plains. John Steinbeck called X "the Mother ____" in The Grapes of Wrath, because of its role in the exodus of climate refugees. After Eisenhower pushed a massive national project in the 1950s, X declined in strategic and commercial importance.
The centenary attracted tourists from around the world in 2026, including one prolific KVizzer.
ID X.
answer_text: X=U.S. Route 66. Steinbeck called it the Mother Road and it is also called the Main Street of America. The route covers 2,448 miles between Chicago, Illinois and Santa Monica, California. It runs through Missouri, Kansas, Oklahoma, Texas, New Mexico, and Arizona. The Interstate system built in the 1950s provided better alternatives to Route 66

question_text:
The producers of the film X Y _______ tried five or six candidate songs before choosing Z. Z fills the classic "I Want" slot of the story. Z topped the charts in over 30 countries and reached number one on the Billboard Global 200 in the summer of 2025.
This February Z became the first X song to win a Grammy Award. In March, it became the first X song to win an Academy Award.
ID X (3 points) and Z (7 points). No points for Y.
answer_text: X=KPop. Z=Golden. The movie is KPop Demon Hunters

question_text:
X got the news this October while attending the Nuremberg Forum, an annual conference hosted by the International Nuremberg Principles Academy.
A few weeks later, Y said in a speech that when he got the news, he asked, "what about me, do they do two of them?"
ID X (7 points) and the news we are discussing (3 points). No points for Y.
answer_text: X=Navi Pillay. Navi Pillay won the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize. She did her press conference in the same room where Hermann Göring was convicted of war crimes and crimes against humanity. Y=Donald Trump. Trump had an epic meltdown with the news that he didn't win a Nobel Peace Prize after starting an illegal war in Iran

question_text:
James Wilson was a Scottish businessman. In 1843, he founded the Economist to champion free trade. When the British Raj replaced Company rule after the War of 1857, Wilson was sent to Kolkata in 1859 as a key member of the brand-new Viceroy's Council. On July 24, 1860 Wilson instituted the policy of X Y in India. The X Y Department of the Government of India still celebrates July 24 as X Y Day. He reportedly refused to escape to Darjeeling for the summer, caught dysentery, and died on August 11.
On Wilson's 165th death anniversary, the Lok Sabha passed the X Bill of 2025. It took about three minutes, with no debate, amid opposition protests. The new act came into force on April 1 this year. Among other changes, it dropped the confusing terms "previous year" and "__________ year" in favor of the new term "Y year".
ID X (7 points) and Y (3 points).
answer_text: X=Income. Y=Tax. When Britain took direct control of India in 1858, it absorbed the East India Company's massive war debts. Instead of paying them off as British debt incurred for a British cause, they taxed India to pay off those debts. The Income Tax Department observes Aykar divas (Income Tax Day) on July 24, marking the anniversary of the 1860 colonial levy

question_text:
Wayne Madsen's first World Cup appearance was in the 2006 FIH Hockey World Cup where he represented South Africa. Twenty years later in 2026, he showed up as the captain of X in a very different World Cup. But he dislocated his shoulder in the very first match against a lowly team and had to leave the field. X suffered a big defeat in that game.
The high point for X in this year's tournament came on February 12. Facing another not-very-good team, X outclassed them in all aspects of the game and won its very first World Cup match. Two Australian-born brothers secured X that lone victory.
ID X.
answer_text: X=Italy. Italy beat Nepal in its second match in the T20 Men's World Cup

question_text:
X took the oath of office as Prime Minister of Y on February 17 this year, becoming the first man to hold that office in about 35 years. He arrived in Y on Christmas Day in 2025, ending a 17-year exile in the United Kingdom.
During his exile, X was convicted in absentia in five cases. The gravest involved a grenade attack on a rival party's rally that killed 24 people. X was sentenced to life imprisonment and later acquitted on appeal in that case.
Both of X's parents led Y at some point their careers.
ID X (7 points) and Y (3 points).
answer_text: X=Tarique Rehman. Y=Bangladesh. Sheikh Hasina and Begum Khaleda Zia took turns as Prime Minister for the last 35 years. Tarique Rehman's father Zia-ur Rehman made himself President of Bangladesh after Sheik Hasina's father Sheikh Mujib-ur Rehman was ousted in a military coup

question_text:
X worked as a programmer at Palm, Blizzard, and AOL. He started writing in his twenties and published work on his own website for years.
X did extensive research into orbital mechanics and botany to write his first published novel. He put it on his website, and some readers requested a Kindle version. He sold the Kindle version for $0.99 (₹94), and it made it to the Kindle bestseller list. The print version then debuted at number 12 on The New York Times bestseller list in 2014.
In 2021, X released his third novel Y. It won the 2022 Audie Award for Audiobook of the Year and a Hugo Award nomination for Best Novel. KVizzers have variously called Y's 2026 movie adaptation: "decent movie: 7/10 for me," "pretty good," "OMG enjoyable wholesome movie," "story thoda timepass laga," "bhai what a movie, I've no words," and "rare instance where the movie is actually better than the book".
ID X (6 points) and Y (4 points).
answer_text: X=Andy Weir. Y=Project Hail Mary. Dhruv Sharma famously said: "PHM will be forever my main girl, while side chicks like Odyssey come and go"

question_text:
Jeremy Hansen grew up on a farm in Ontario and joined the Royal Canadian Air Cadets at age 12. He got his pilot license at 17 and went on to fly the CF-18 Hornet fighter, achieving the rank of colonel in the Royal Canadian Air Force.
Hansen turned 50 this year. In April, he realized a life-long dream, and in the process set several records. He is the only Canadian, and the first person without an American passport, to do something. What?
Looking for a specific answer.
answer_text: Hansen is the first Canadian, and the first non-American, to travel beyond earth orbit. Along with his Artemis II crewmates, he is one of the four people who have traveled the farthest distance from earth in human history. Hansen took this picture from Artemis II

question_text:
X was selected to lead the Y this year, which deeply upset conservative influencers. X is a natural-born American citizen. After conservatives threatened to boycott the Y in protest, Turning Point USA came up with an "All-American" alternative, implying that X was somehow less than American. They announced a lineup with names like Kid Rock, Brantley Gilbert, Lee Brice, and Gabby Barrett. J.D. Vance promoted this as a "fantastic lineup" in February.
ID X (5 points) and Y (5 points).
answer_text: X=Benito Antonio Martínez Ocasio, aka Bad Bunny. Y=Superbowl half-time show. Bad Bunny's show got over 128 million live viewers, while TPUSA's alternative stream got about 5 million live viewers

question_text:
X's first-ever knock-out stage win in the Women's World Cup was in 2023. They then kept going and beat England 1-0 in Sydney in the final of that World Cup. Celebrations of this joyous event in X were marred by the inappropriate behavior of a leader of X's federation for this sport.
This year, X became the only country in the sport's history to hold both the Women's and Men's World Cup titles concurrently.
Prior to 2023, Y was the only country to have won both the Men's and the Women's World Cups in this sport, but Y did not hold both titles at the same time.
ID X (6 points) and Y (4 points).
answer_text: X=Spain. Y=Germany. Germany won the FIFA Women's World Cup in 2003 and 2007 and the FIFA Men's World Cup in 1954, 1974, 1990, and 2014

question_text:
Rerum Novarum ("of new things") is a Latin treatise published in 1891. It charts out a middle path for society, between what it portrays as the extremes of state socialism and laissez-faire capitalism. It was issued in the name of X. It advocates for private property, a limited state, living wages, the right for labor to organize, and class cooperation rather than class warfare. Christian Democratic parties across Europe can trace their ideologies back to this text.
When Robert Prevost took a new job recently, he chose the name X because of this major influence X had on how European society adapted to the Industrial Revolution.
This May he issued his own manifesto for how society should adapt to the AI Revolution. He signed it exactly 135 years to the day after Rerum Novarum was signed. It is unclear whether his influence on this age will match X's influence on his.
ID X.
answer_text: X=Pope Leo XIII. Robert Prevost became Pope Leo XIV, because he wants to have the same influence on this age that Pope Leo XIII had on his age. Magnifica Humanitas, the encyclical Pope Leo XIV issued, argues that artificial intelligence must serve human dignity and the common good, not concentrate power in a few tech giants, and warns that, left unchecked, AI risks widening inequality, weakening democracy and undermining what it means to be human

question_text:
This is the beginning of a letter sent on February 28 this year by the new CEO of X to its shareholders. This is the first time since 1965 that the CEO's annual shareholder letter at X has been written by someone other than Y.
ID X (5 points) and Y (5 points).
[Image: redacted letter excerpt: "[X] Inc. To My Fellow [X] Shareholders, [Y] is arguably the greatest [___] of all time, with generations benefiting from his [___] acumen. He has also been a remarkable CEO, executing his vision of building a great insurance business since the acquisition of National Indemnity in 1967, and deploying the float to make successful [___] across major sectors of the economy, concentrating in the U.S. (To [Y]'s great frustration, this letter begins with these observations – yet we all know they are true.)"]
answer_text: X=Berkshire Hathaway. Y=Warren Buffett. Greg Abel became CEO on January 1 this year after Buffett retired. Buffett stayed as Chairman of the company's Board of Directors
